annotation.authors_or_issuer: Department of Communications and Digital Technologies (South Africa)
key_provisions_or_claims: First step toward a National AI Policy; comments invited by 29 November 2024
Nine strategic pillars including talent, digital infrastructure, R&D, public sector implementation
Ethical AI guidelines emphasising human-centred AI that augments rather than replaces human decisions
Pillars on privacy and data protection, safety and security, transparency and explainability, fairness and bias mitigation
Uses a futures approach (push of present, pull of future, weight of past) to set AI objectives
annotation.summary_en: South Africa's October 2024 National AI Policy Framework, issued by the DCDT for public comment, is a first step toward a national AI policy. It sets objectives and nine pillars covering talent, infrastructure, R&D, public sector use, ethics, privacy, safety, transparency and fairness, promoting inclusive, human-centred AI growth.
